main_text.l: SCINDITVR HVMANVM STV-dia in contraria vulgus.

l.i: Laudis opes, dotesq; tagi, venerisq; latebras, Sectatur stolidum nunc ubicunq; genus: Quæ bona de cœlo CHRISTI quoq; sanguine partæ, Dat Deus, hæc amens spernere munde soles!

page.notes: The engraving (not transcribed as text) shows a winged cupid pushing a heart-marked ball, a man in a plumed hat holding out a hand toward a rope and a pedestal with a pile of coins, a sword on a pedestal, and two small figures at left. Doubtful: "tagi" and "munde soles" (printed with a tight space, possibly "mundesoles"); the verse line "Quæ bona de cœlo" is in italic with CHRISTI in capitals as printed.
